$comment: D-LIR-AAPCS64-CALL-MIXING-LONG-DOUBLE-AND-DOUBLE-ARGS-REFUSED: a call passing a `long double` AND a `float`/`double` places every argument in its own register. Under AAPCS64 (aarch64 Linux) a `long double` is IEEE binary128, a whole Q register drawn from the SAME floating-point argument sequence (NSRN) as `float` and `double`; DSS marshalled the binary128 arguments in MIR->LIR and placed every other argument in `lir_callconv`, two walks with no shared cursor, so a mix was REFUSED at the caller — "MIR opcode '<deferred>' is not yet lowered", debug and release, ✔MEASURED at `7df54cc1` on all six shapes here. Now ONE placer: the marshalled argument keeps its position in the call's operand list as the register it was loaded into, so the one `ArgCursors` walk hands every later FP argument the next register, and the marshal loads carry a register constraint so a double live across them is never allocated the register they write. Seven shapes, exit 11..17: the long double first, second, interleaved with a float and integers, a mix whose last double overflows onto the stack after eight FP registers (its placement counts the long double), an indirect call, a long-double RESULT, and (aarch64 only) one long double beside THIRTY doubles all live at the call, so the allocator must use the low FP registers for some — the shape that proves the marshal's constraint is load-bearing. aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 run it to 42 at -O0 and -O2 under qemu-aarch64. Every value is exact in binary32/64, x87 and binary128, so the x86_64 (x87 `long double` on the stack) and Apple arm64 (`long double` IS `double`) arms run the same file as the control. RED-ON-DISABLE, ✔MEASURED 2026-09-19: leave the marshalled argument out of the call's operand list again (and drop the refusal) -> the aarch64 arm returns 11 at debug and release (the double lands in the long double's register); keep it listed but mint no constraint for the marshal loads -> this file exits 17 on the aarch64 debug arm (the thirty-double shape: a double parked in v0 and overwritten by the long double's load) while every other shape still passes. The x86_64 arms are the control and do not take the thirty-double shape: there an x87 `long double` rides the stack and a double overflowing after it is the separate, recorded D-FC12-VARIADIC-OVERFLOW-FIXED-AGGREGATE-STACK-ARGS.
